subject_matter: porcelain, scepter, shou roundel, bats, clouds, double happiness character, crane, rockwork, flowering prunus branches, jadeite imitation
description_block:
A Chinese Porcelain Imitating Jadeite  Ruyi  Scepter, Late Qing/Republic Period 晚清-民國 仿翡翠釉雲蝠雙喜紋瓷如意 
 
 Late Qing/Republic Period (1912-1949) 
 The heavily potted porcelain scepter is finely molded in high relief on top of the  ruyi  head centered with a  shou  roundel enclosed by winged bats and auspicious clouds, the raised oblong-shaped center section and the quatrefoil end of the shaft each molded with a  shaugnxi  (double happiness) character against an interlocking T ground; the rest of the handle with crane above rockwork and flowering prunus branches. The scepter is enameled overall in mottled blue-green and white in imitation of jadeite.  
 Length 17 3/4 in., 45.1 cm.

A Chinese Cinnabar Lacquer on Metal Covered  Ding  Vessel, Late Qing/Republic Period 晚清/民國 銅胎剔紅龍紋鼎

A Japanese Mixed-Metal Inset Lacquer Stationary Box,  Bunko,  Meiji-Taisho Period
